entries.en: That is sort of what I'd heard about your people. I guess you're not in any one place long enough for people to get to know you.
That is an ignorant opinion. Quarian explorers have uncovered more mass relays than any other race!
I am glad that some still remember the contributions my people have made.
It is natural for people to dislike rootless wanderers. If quarians would just settle another homeworld, you would not run into such concerns.
Perspective is a wonderful thing. Wait until their homeworld gets wiped out.
I'd love to see what the Normandy can do in a fight.
The Normandy isn't built for a stand-up fight. I'd rather rely on the IES than the shields.
How so? The Normandy is built for stealth, not combat.
Only an idiot hopes for combat while flying in a stealth ship.
But the stealth drive adds a new tactical level to space combat as we know it. Surprise attacks, undetected flanking maneuvers...
I don't know, Garrus. I'd rather not be the first one up the ladder in terms of figuring out new tactics.
I don't know, Garrus. I'd rather not be the first one up the ladder when it comes to new tactics.
I had forgotten the turian appreciation for tactics and strategy. With respect, I hope we avoid ship-to-ship combat entirely.
If it comes to a fight, I'd prefer a flotilla ship. It's easier to trust what you've worked on yourself.
This isn't a strategy simulation. If those new tactics don't work, we're salvage.
So tell me, who'd win in a fight between you and Shepard?
What? Commander Shepard is my superior officer. I can't imagine us ever having to fight.
You can't? That's why Shepard's your superior officer. And that's why Shepard would win.
Do krogan size up everyone for a fight, even friends and allies?
That question smacks of impertinence. Commander Shepard is a Spectre with a distinguished service record.
So was Saren. Think about it.
It must be nice to be back in civilization after so long in those Prothean ruins.
You must welcome civilization after spending such a long time in the Prothean ruins.
You must welcome civilization after so long a time in the Prothean ruins.
Being in the city must feel good after digging through rocks at that Prothean ruin.
No. Cities and stations were always my mother's area of comfort. I actually enjoy the solitude of dig sites.
When this is all over, you'll be able to go back to your rocks and ruins for as long as you'd like.
I don't think I could handle that. Eden Prime was as quiet and rustic as I'd ever want.
After seeing so many asari come through the Citadel, I assumed your people preferred large cities. I apologize.
The ship I grew up on was always full of noise and people. The solitude of a dig site would drive me crazy.
I'm surprised. I've never met an asari who didn't prefer clean clothes and a hot bath.
Congratulations, Shepard. Heard they made you a Spectre.
I'm glad somebody got the Council to see Saren for what he really is.
I resigned from C-Sec after the Council ignored my investigation. I was sick of all the politics.
You're the only one who seems to be doing anything about Saren. Let me come with you.
Commander Shepard. Have you reconsidered? Do you want me to come with you?
All turians are not the same. I'm not like Saren.
I couldn't prove it in my investigation, but I knew what was really going on. Saren's a traitor to the Council, and a disgrace to my people!
Just think about it, Shepard. If you change your mind, come look for me in the C-Sec Academy.
You won't regret this, Shepard.
I appreciate that, Garrus.
Something I can help you with, Garrus?
You're a turian. Why do you want to bring him down?
I don't need a turian shooting me in the back when I least expect it.
I don't want you on this mission.
Welcome aboard, Garrus.
You've made your case.
Why do you hate Saren?
You made your case.
Commander Shepard? Sorry to bother you. This is Lieutenant Girard down in the docking bay.
There's a woman here, uh... She was rescued from batarian slavers a few weeks ago. She's from Mindoir. I guess she was taken. In the raid on your town.
Not really. She's a little messed up.
Understood, Commander. But she's barricaded herself in the docking bay with a gun. If you have time, we could use your help talking her down.
Yes ma'am. Sorry, ma'am.
Yes sir. Sorry, sir.
She got free somehow. Grabbed a gun from one of my guys.
Now she's holed up here in the docking bay. She, uh-- She says she wants to die.
I hoped you'd talk to her. It's a long shot, but you went through the same thing. The raid. I figured maybe you could talk her out of her tree.
I, uh-- Understood, Commander. We'll try to handle her ourselves. Sorry to bother you.
Anything you can do would be great. I don't want to-- She's been through enough. I'll have my men stand by for you.
She's been a slave for the past 13 years? Is she all right?
I'm busy right now, Lieutenant.
You mean she was taken in the raid that killed my parents.
I'm on my way, Lieutenant. Sit tight.
Lieutenant, if she wants to die, let her die. That's her choice to make.
I'm not trained for that, but I'll do what I can.
Not now.
When my parents died.
Let her do it.
I'll try.
Khalisah bint Sinan Al-Jilani, Westerlund News. Would you answer a few questions for our viewers?
People back home have heard a lot of wild stories about you, Commander.
I can give you the chance to set the record straight. What do you say?
You've been given a unique position to represent our race. People want to get a sense of how you'll do that.
Your choice, Shepard.
I'm sure our viewers will understand.
Humans have been trying to get the respect of the galactic community for 26 years. With that in mind, what are your feelings on being the first human Spectre?
Some have said your appointment is the Citadel "throwing humans a bone."
Some believe that without firm action on our part, the Council will continue to treat us like "poor relations."
But there's a difference between protecting human interests and Citadel interests.
Have you encountered any situations where the Citadel asked you to place its needs before the needs of Earth?
You can't just walk away, Commander. The public has a right to know!
Isn't it true you're just a shill for the Council?
You really do believe that, don't you?
I think our viewers will be glad to hear that, Commander.
You son of a bitch!
You bitch!
I'll make sure everyone in the Alliance sees that! Your career is over!
That's not quite an answer, Commander.
You've been given command of an advanced human warship for your missions. Is there anything you'd like to say about it?
So the turians have knowledge of the Normandy that is being kept secret from the Alliance public?
That's gratifying. Many defeatist officers claim that the Alliance can't compete with the naval power of, say, the turians.
Some members of that crew are aliens, as I recall.
Do you think it was appropriate to hand Earth's most advanced warship over to the Citadel?
Human, yes. But you do work for the Citadel now, Commander.
No offense intended, Commander. I'm sure you have to follow the orders of your superiors. Of course, now your superiors are aliens.
So this was only to help you. In your new job working for the Citadel.
Speaking of your new job, did the Council order you to sabotage human research concern on Noveria?
That's a surprising revelation, Commander. We've had nothing but stonewalling from Binary Helix.
It's gratifying to see someone who'll make tough choices to protect the lives of humans.
So you were there on a mission from the Council? That's very interesting.
In your opinion, Commander, who should be held responsible for the failure of the colony on Feros?
If memory serves, ExoGeni mainly invests in worlds where alien artifacts might be uncovered.
It's curious how often these "peace-loving" aliens attack us first. First the turians, and now this species.
I suppose you'll have to accept the judgment of history, then.
Given your recent experiences, do you think humanity will ever get the respect it deserves from the galactic community?
You're an idealist, Commander. But a sincere one. I hope you're right.
I hope they remember that when they pass the next defense budget.
One last question, Commander.
Rumors back home say you're tracking a "rogue Spectre" named Saren. Do you have any comment on that?
That's... surprising, Commander. The official line says Eden Prime was attacked by rogue synthetics.
Strong words. It's a good time for strong words.
Good luck in your mission.
Don't worry. We'll find out. The eyes of Earth are on you. Don't let us down.
Thank you for your time, Commander Shepard.
I'm not in the mood, Miss Al-Jilani.
What sort of questions?
What do you want to know?
I don't have time to justify myself to your viewers. I have a galaxy to save. Excuse me.
So long as you understand that I may not be able to answer all questions.
The Spectres represent the best of every species in the galaxy. To be asked to join them is an honor.
We all know it should have happened years ago. I hope the Council realizes that we won't sit at the kids' table forever.
I try to keep in mind that it's just another form of duty. I still wear a uniform.
Hold on. It's pretty clear you have an agenda here. I'm not going to be part of it. Excuse me.
The Council is concerned with the needs of whole galactic community. We're part of that community now. Our needs are on their agenda, but we're one of many.
I think they know not to ask me to work against my own people.
I've had enough of your snide insinuations.
The Spectre charter allows me to complete my missions any way I see fit.
Actually, the Normandy was co-developed by human and turian engineers. Its design incorporates many innovations. All of which are classified, I'm afraid.
The Normandy is a triumph of human engineering. Like our development of fighter carriers, it shows other races that we're able to think "outside the box."
Many details are still classified, I'm afraid. I can tell you she's a fine ship, and has the best crew I've ever served with.
I wasn't aware it had been "handed over" to anyone. I'm in command, and last I checked, I'm human. Same goes for my crew.
Ms. Al-Jilani, I wear the Alliance uniform. And if you think anyone other than me says where the Normandy can go, you're sadly mistaken.
The Normandy has only been loaned to the Citadel. It's a legal technicality that allows me to use her in my new role as Spectre.
The Council had nothing to do with it. There was an accident at Binary Helix labs. In the interest of protecting the company's confidentiality, I can't say more.
I made that call to save myself, my crew, and the inhabitants of Noveria. And I'd do it again.
I'm afraid I can't discuss the details of my missions.
ExoGeni Corp. settled Feros knowing full well the danger it posed to colonists. You could say they were banking on it.
I can't discuss the particulars, but a previously-undocumented species was discovered in the ruins.
Me. I resolved the situation to the best of my ability. The results weren't all I hoped for. But I still don't see what I could have done differently.
Respect's a funny thing. People always assume they deserve it. The truth is, respect is earned. And I firmly believe we can earn it.
Ever read Machiavelli? He believed it's better to be feared than loved. We build a few dozen more dreadnoughts, I guarantee we'll be respected.
Saren instigated the attack on our colony at Eden Prime. Once his involvement was proven to the Council, I was assigned to bring him in.
For a long time, the Council sat on their hands with regard to Saren. I have to wonder where their thumbs were.
I'm afraid I can't comment on whatever my current assignment may or may not be.
Go away.
Depends.
I say get stuffed.
Some topics are classified.
Honored.
